report.summary: Chunk 2 of cancel.py defines Windows job object structures, kernel32 prototypes, console_ctrl_available, _win_error, and _resume_all_threads.
risks: _resume_all_threads | medium | Uses CreateToolhelp32Snapshot with 0 as th32ProcessID; this enumerates all threads system-wide, not just the target PID. Could cause performance issues or race conditions on high-thread-count systems. | Verify that the snapshot is filtered efficiently or document that PID 0 is intended for system-wide enumeration.

handoff.purpose: Define Windows job object and thread structures, kernel32 function prototypes, and helper functions for console control and thread resumption.

symbols.name: _JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION
symbols.note: ctypes Structure for job object basic limit information.

symbols.name: _JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION
symbols.note: ctypes Structure for job object extended limit information, includes _JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION and IO counters.

symbols.name: _THREADENTRY32
symbols.note: ctypes Structure for thread entry used in toolhelp snapshot.

symbols.name: console_ctrl_available
symbols.note: Returns whether console control events can be delivered (stage 1). On Windows, checks GetConsoleProcessList; on non-Windows, returns True.

symbols.name: _win_error
symbols.note: Creates CancellationUnavailable exception with GetLastError code.

symbols.name: _resume_all_threads
symbols.note: Resumes all threads of a given PID using toolhelp snapshot and OpenThread/ResumeThread.

claims.text: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent needs the caller to own a console; a process started without one (pythonw, a service, some IDE runners) can only ever reach stage 2.
claims.why: The claim references stage 2 and console ownership requirements not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Resume every thread of `pid`; returns how many resume calls succeeded.
claims.why: The code iterates threads with matching pid, calls ResumeThread in a while loop, increments resumed on success, and returns resumed.

claims.text: Popen closes the initial thread handle before returning, so the only way back to a CREATE_SUSPENDED child is a thread snapshot.
claims.why: The claim refers to Popen behavior not present in this chunk.

observations.what: CreateToolhelp32Snapshot is called with th32ProcessID = 0, which according to MSDN enumerates all processes. This may be inefficient.
The while loop in _resume_all_threads continues until ResumeThread returns (DWORD)-1 (0xFFFFFFFF) or previous <= 1. This could loop many times if a thread is suspended multiple times.
